items.problem: The bootstrap omitted UWP project inputs linked from outside -Source.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 inventoried only the physical source subtree and ignored evaluated Link metadata.
items.change: Locate Visual Studio MSBuild, evaluate safe Compile/Page/ApplicationDefinition/Content/Resource/None items, and copy external linked XAML/C#/resource/asset inputs to their Link destinations before namespace rewrite and mapping. Skip legacy linked AssemblyInfo.cs and fail rather than emit an incomplete inventory when linked-item evaluation is unavailable.
items.expected_effect: Shared App/MainPage/styles/assets become first-class mapped inputs instead of being manually reconstructed, preserving explicit theme and shell resources.
items.falsifiable_check: On TextSuggestion, bootstrap reports 12 linked project items copied and App.xaml, MainPage.xaml, Styles/Styles.xaml, and both SDK shell assets exist in the target.

items.problem: The documented build loop used nonexistent winapp build and omitted common SDK-style XAML diagnostics.
items.root_cause: Build prose was outdated; project/XAML guidance did not make implicit Page items or markup-extension syntax explicit.
items.change: Use native platform-qualified dotnet build throughout and add NETSDK1022 duplicate-Page and WMC0503 property-element x:Bind recipes.
items.expected_effect: The normal build produces the layout expected by Test-AppLaunch and agents resolve these two deterministic errors without exploratory retries.
items.falsifiable_check: A re-run contains no rejected winapp build command, no unavailable launch caused by bin\Debug layout, and fixes NETSDK1022/WMC0503 from the named recipes if encountered.

items.problem: NavigationView shell substitution preserved behavior but changed theme, Settings visibility, pane geometry, title-bar chrome, and heading wrapping.
items.evidence: discrepancies.json entries 1-3; migration-score.json marks all three features partial at score 50
items.root_cause: The existing navigation anchor specifies event wiring but not the source shell's visible contract or replacement-control defaults.
items.change: Extend the existing NavigationView anchor with source-derived RequestedTheme, IsSettingsVisible, OpenPaneLength, text wrapping/width, and title-bar/template-chrome rules.
items.expected_effect: Shell replacements retain source visuals while still using WinUI 3 navigation behavior.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, App.xaml retains RequestedTheme=Dark, no Settings navigation item appears, pane/heading geometry matches the source, and the three visual/layout discrepancies are absent.
